exactText: The U.S. will be the principal source of global risk this year.
sourceQuote: The U.S. will be the principal source of global risk this year.
normalizedClaim: The United States will be the principal source of global geopolitical risk in 2026.
resolutionCriteria: Eurasia Group / GZERO assessments and independent risk indices (e.g., geopolitical risk indexes from major banks or think tanks) ranking the U.S. as the top driver of global uncertainty throughout 2026.

exactText: Trump’s return to office will unleash an “unmanaged decoupling in the world’s most important geopolitical relationship.”
sourceQuote: unmanaged decoupling in the world’s most important geopolitical relationship.
normalizedClaim: Donald Trump’s second term will trigger unmanaged decoupling between the United States and China.
resolutionCriteria: Measurable increase in trade barriers, technology restrictions, investment bans, or diplomatic rupture between the U.S. and China during 2025–2026, documented by official policy announcements and trade data.

exactText: The competition between the United States and China to develop AI and deploy it globally poses the biggest threat to the two countries’ currently constructive relations.
sourceQuote: poses the biggest threat to the two countries’ currently constructive relations.
normalizedClaim: The U.S.-China AI race is the biggest threat to the current détente between the two countries.
resolutionCriteria: Breakdown or significant deterioration of U.S.-China diplomatic/economic guardrails specifically linked to AI competition (export controls, sanctions, military AI incidents) by end of 2027, as reported by primary diplomatic sources.

exactText: China has mastered the “electric stack” that powers EVs, batteries, drones, robotics, and AI—emerging as the world’s first “electrostate.”
normalizedClaim: China has become the world’s first “electrostate” by mastering the electric technology stack (EVs, batteries, drones, robotics, AI power infrastructure).
resolutionCriteria: China’s global market share leadership in EVs, batteries, rare-earth processing, and related clean-tech supply chains remaining dominant through 2026–2028, per IEA, BloombergNEF, or equivalent data.

exactText: The closer Ukraine comes to humiliating the Kremlin, the greater the risk that Putin might turn in desperation to a tactical nuclear strike or more aggressive and direct attacks on frontline NATO countries
sourceQuote: the greater the risk that Putin might turn in desperation to a tactical nuclear strike or more aggressive and direct attacks on frontline NATO countries
normalizedClaim: If Ukraine approaches a humiliating defeat of Russia, the risk of Putin resorting to a tactical nuclear strike or direct attacks on NATO countries will increase significantly.
resolutionCriteria: Observable escalation involving tactical nuclear threats/use or direct Russian military action against NATO territory correlated with major Ukrainian battlefield gains, as documented by official statements and independent verification by 2027.

exactText: AI could harden autocracies and fray democracies, flipping the shape back toward an inverted J whose stable slope now favors closed systems.
sourceQuote: AI could harden autocracies and fray democracies
normalizedClaim: Advanced AI will tend to strengthen closed/autocratic political systems relative to open democracies over time.
resolutionCriteria: Comparative political science metrics (Freedom House, V-Dem, or equivalent) showing relative strengthening of authoritarian regimes’ control capabilities versus democratic resilience linked to AI deployment by 2035.

exactText: A G-Zero world is an era when no one power or group of powers is both willing and able to drive a global agenda and maintain international order. ... The result is a uniquely dangerous period of world history on par with the 1930s or the early Cold War.
sourceQuote: A G-Zero world is an era when no one power or group of powers is both willing and able to drive a global agenda
normalizedClaim: The world has entered a G-Zero era in which no single power or coalition is both willing and able to maintain international order, creating a uniquely dangerous period.
resolutionCriteria: Continued absence of effective global leadership on major crises (trade, security, climate, pandemic preparedness) through 2027, as evidenced by failed multilateral initiatives and rising conflict metrics.

exactText: There’s clearly a much higher likelihood of direct military confrontation now between the U.S. and Russia. The U.S. and Iran. The U.S. and North Korea.
sourceQuote: There’s clearly a much higher likelihood of direct military confrontation now between the U.S. and Russia.
normalizedClaim: The likelihood of direct military confrontation between the U.S. and Russia (and also with Iran and North Korea) is substantially higher than in recent prior periods.
resolutionCriteria: Occurrence or narrowly averted direct U.S.-Russia military engagement (beyond Ukraine proxy conflict), or equivalent with Iran/North Korea, documented by official military reports by 2028.

exactText: It’s probably inevitable that the United States is going to look more like China in the way it deals with AI. ... the US government will demand some level of direct influence and control over them.
sourceQuote: the United States is going to look more like China in the way it deals with AI. ... the US government will demand some level of direct influence and control
normalizedClaim: The U.S. government will move toward greater direct influence and control over frontier AI companies, resembling Chinese-style industrial policy and oversight.
resolutionCriteria: Enactment of significant U.S. federal legislation or executive actions granting the government equity stakes, kill-switch authority, or licensing control over leading AI labs by 2030.

exactText: 2026 is a tipping point year. ... the U.S. is unwinding its own global order.
sourceQuote: 2026 is a tipping point year. ... the U.S. is unwinding its own global order.
normalizedClaim: 2026 marks a tipping point in which the United States actively unwinds the post-WWII international order it previously led.
resolutionCriteria: Observable U.S. policy actions in 2026 that substantially reduce commitment to existing alliances, trade regimes, or multilateral institutions, as documented by official statements and institutional membership/funding changes.
